articles.title: Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
articles.originalTitle: Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
articles.excerpt: A card-skimming script was planted on the online stores of Lascana, Samsonite, American Tourister, Revolve and FWRD in the week before Black Friday. After our reports to affected companies, all have had the script removed (on November 24th or 25th) ahead of Black Friday. We observed it in action on one of the five websites: Lascana, where it sent our test card's details to a 3rd party. We believe the script was built to take a card number, expiry and security code, along with a user's name, address, phone and email, and send them to malefactors as a user entered their payment credentials. It did this before the store checked the payment, so a card could be taken even if the order was declined or cancelled, and nothing would look wrong to the shopper. Across all of these sites, we do not know how many, if any, shopper details or payment credentials may have been captured.

Dla mnie na zachodzie/ Rozlałeś tęczę blasków promienistą;/ Przede mną gasisz w lazurowej wodzie/ Gwiazdę ognistą…/ Choć mi tak niebo Ty złocisz i morze,/ Smutno mi, Boże!”. Scientists analyzing more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep-sea fish and shrimp in the Gulf discovered troubling signs of extinction risk in every species examined.

articles.title: These bizarre prehistoric mammals may have been misunderstood for 150 years
articles.originalTitle: These bizarre prehistoric mammals may have been misunderstood for 150 years
articles.excerpt: Giant horned mammals that emerged shortly after the extinction of the dinosaurs may have had far fewer physical differences between males and females than scientists once believed. The discovery challenges a classic example of sexual dimorphism and raises questions about how historical biases have shaped our understanding of extinct animals.

articles.originalTitle: This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain
articles.excerpt: A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most. In a randomized clinical trial involving 50 middle-aged adults with obesity, researchers found that taking the supplement daily for four weeks increased blood flow to the brain during a challenging memory task, particularly in a region involved in working memory.
